title: CardCorpus sets of a catalog
description: Every set of one catalog (`sets/english.json`, `sets/japanese.json` and so on, one a catalog), with what a list of sets needs: its name, era, type, language, release date, card count, set code, logo and symbol. A set is one product's card list, such as Base Set, a promo series or a deck. They come era by era and then by release date. There is no list of every catalog's sets: index.json's `catalogs` names the catalogs, in the order lists use. Each set's cards are in sets/{id}.json (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#sets).

catalog.description: The catalog these sets are in.

setCount.description: How many sets; always present, 0 included.

sets.description: Every set of the catalog, era by era and then by release date.

id.description: The set's id. Treat it as opaque: it never changes once published.

catalog.description: The catalog the set belongs to.

name.description: The set's name as it prints it, in its language. Where no source gives the printed name yet, its English name (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#names).

englishName.description: The set's name in English, on every set: "Expansion Pack (Base Set)" (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#names).

era.description: Its era, by pointer, which stays when the era is renamed.

$kind.description: What the pointer points at: `era`. index.json's `pointers` say where to find it (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#pointers).

name.description: A copy of the target's own `name`.

englishName.description: A copy of the target's own `englishName`.

type.description: What the set is, by how its cards reached people.

language.description: The language its cards are printed in: its catalog's, apart from a box like the Pikachu World Collection, which holds cards in several (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#foreign-prints).

position.description: Its place among its catalog's sets of one release date, where the data orders them.

line.description: The line the set is one part of, where several of our sets came out as one product or range of products (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#lines).

$kind.description: What the pointer points at: `line`. index.json's `pointers` say where to find it (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#pointers).

name.description: A copy of the target's own `name`.

part.description: The words that tell this set from the line's others: "Blaziken Tech" for "2004 World Championships Deck: Blaziken Tech", "Latias" for "EX Trainer Kit Latias".

printedTotal.description: The total its card numbers print (the 102 of 4/102), where they print one.

actualTotal.description: How many cards the set has by its own count, secret cards included, where known.

cardCount.description: How many cards the set has in its `cards`; always present, 0 included.

released.description: When the set came out, as precisely as is known (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#release-dates).

inferred.description: `true` where the date is an estimate: no page dates the set's print in its language, so its year is borrowed from another language's print (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#release-dates). Absent otherwise.

printedCode.description: The set code and language mark its cards print where they name their set, as printed (in the set code's letter case): "PBL FR", "M6a F", "CSV3C", "SV9a". Null where the cards print no code of their own (Base Set); absent where nobody has checked yet (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#printed-codes).

symbol.description: The set symbol, the small mark its cards print (an icon a source gives for a set that prints none).

linkCount.description: How many links the set has to other sets; always present, 0 included.
